topic: Face-complete endpoint-prior saddles and the answer-open indexability correspondence for asymmetric nonsmooth partial identification: solve the compact non-centrosymmetric polyhedral Gaussian endpoint game over all measurable randomized rules; characterize every saddle, classify the full optimal correspondence into all one-index, coexistence, or no one-index cases, construct convergent primal-dual certificates without a complexity-rate claim, and prove tie-uniform perturbation plus LAN/Le Cam transfer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: a legal 2D witness has value 2/3 and both constant one-index and tanh-perturbed non-one-index optima. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: a non-tautological general indexability criterion. EARLY KILL TEST: interval certification of an unbalanced-prior non-halfspace case.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the minimax-regret value and the complete set of saddle pairs for compact non-centrosymmetric polyhedral Gaussian endpoint games with directionally differentiable lower and upper welfare bounds, allowing every measurable randomized rule.

source_refs.claim: Section 6 leaves directional differentiability without centrosymmetry for future research after solving the two assumptions separately.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Exact finite-sample minimax-regret optimality over all decision rules is obtained for Gaussian experiments under a convex, centrosymmetric parameter space.
source_refs.author: Kohei Yata
source_refs.venue: arXiv; revise and resubmit at Review of Economic Studies

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two available reductions use incompatible geometric devices. In the differentiable asymmetric case, first-order conditions make the endpoint gradients collinear and reduce the game to one dimension. In the nonsmooth case, centrosymmetry supplies paired endpoint faces and an antipodal least-favorable prior. With both asymmetry and polyhedral nonsmoothness, neither collinearity nor paired faces is available, so the existing embedding and two-point-prior arguments neither prove a sharp value nor exhaust the saddle set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A value formula and saddle-set characterization giving endpoint-face support reduction, necessary-and-sufficient primal and dual equalizer conditions, and existence and completeness over all measurable rules and probability priors.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation reduces a partially identified treatment problem to a Gaussian endpoint game and isolates the geometric assumption that makes the game solvable.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sampling uncertainty and partial identification interact -> localization produces a Gaussian endpoint game -> two separate regularity regimes are solved -> the joint asymmetric-nonsmooth regime remains open.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a modulus-of-continuity extremal pair to construct a least-favorable prior, derive its Bayes response, and match Bayes and worst-case regret.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves global optimality among all measurable rules for the same Gaussian treatment-choice game, but its antipodal pair must be replaced by a face-complete asymmetric prior.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize minimax rules through Bayes responses to least-favorable priors and use equalizer identities to expose multiplicity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target has the same infinite-dimensional rule space and endpoint regret loss, but requires asymmetric face support rather than symmetric pairs.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer a solved Gaussian decision through a best-regular reduced-form estimator and covariance substitution to a locally asymptotically minimax feasible rule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the joint Gaussian game is solved, this is the nearest route to an implementable rule and a local asymptotic regret guarantee.

open_problems.open_problem: Find a non-tautological geometric criterion that classifies a compact asymmetric polyhedral Gaussian endpoint game according to whether every optimum is one-index, one-index and genuinely non-one-index optima coexist, or no one-index optimum exists.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves multiplicity and special-case failure of linear threshold rules while selecting only one optimum in an interpretable one-index class.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: The separated smooth-asymmetric and nonsmooth-centrosymmetric results exhibit an optimal efficient-index rule but do not characterize every optimum.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.excerpt: Randomized policies ... and sample-minimax decision rules are outside the formal claims.
when the coherent regret selector equals the pointwise-envelope selector, in observable capacity inequalities

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existence of a one-index Bayes response does not constrain the whole minimax correspondence: mixtures and perturbations can preserve every binding risk while adding dependence orthogonal to the advertised index, whereas failure of threshold rules does not exclude randomized one-index rules. The web literature certifies selected constructions using symmetry or collinearity, and the prior diagnostic proposal reaches only nested deterministic thresholds and explicitly excludes randomized policies. Neither source turns the normal fan of all active faces and all dual optimal priors into a necessary-and-sufficient factorization criterion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient condition stated in endpoint-face normals, covariance geometry, and least-favorable-prior support that partitions the game into the all-one-index, coexistence, and no-one-index cases.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames multiplicity as economically substantive and separates existence, uniqueness, randomization, and restricted-class optimality.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Partial identification makes conventional uniqueness fail -> globally minimax rules can behave differently -> selected refinements reveal only part of the correspondence -> classify when the full correspondence can be compressed to one index.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine Gaussian bounded completeness, Bayes-response formulas, and perturbations preserving binding regret to prove uniqueness or multiplicity statements.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those tools distinguish an exhibited index rule from factorization of every rule in the optimal correspondence.

method_exemplars.technique: Recover an optimal linear index from a modulus extremizer and certify it using a least-favorable two-point experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the canonical positive indexability theorem whose ingredients must be tested for necessity outside centrosymmetry.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the efficient index and covariance, select the threshold or randomized regime, and establish local asymptotic minimaxity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A usable classification must identify which estimated index, if any, transfers back to the original causal decision problem.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether a compact two-dimensional asymmetric polyhedral Gaussian endpoint game admits an interval-certifiable unbalanced least-favorable prior for which every minimax rule has curved non-halfspace decision geometry and fails to factor through any single linear index.

source_refs.claim: Exact asymmetric-regret solutions for point-identified normal, Bernoulli, and bounded-outcome experiments retain threshold-type structure.
source_refs.author: Aleksey Tetenov

source_refs.claim: A symmetric partial-identification example excludes linear threshold rules but still has randomized optima based on one linear index.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Current exact limit-game solutions use either collinear affine endpoints or centrosymmetry and explicitly leave asymmetric directionally differentiable bounds open.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, and Jörg Stoye

open_problems.why_unsolved: Known exact constructions reduce Nature to symmetric or collinear two-point support, making the Bayes likelihood ratio a function of one Gaussian projection. Under asymmetric polyhedral faces, an unbalanced multi-face prior instead gives a difference of Gaussian mixtures whose zero set can be curved. The located literature has no rigorous low-dimensional example showing that this geometry survives global minimax verification and excludes every alternative one-index optimizer; accordingly, the claimed value-2/3 constant/tanh witness remains presolve evidence, not an established fact.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either explicit rational polyhedral data with interval bounds on all required Gaussian integrals and a closed primal-dual gap proving an unbalanced saddle and impossibility of every representation d(y)=g(w'y), or a two-dimensional impossibility theorem ruling out such a witness.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the clearest economic motivation for unequal penalties and treats asymmetry as primitive to treatment-choice regret.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: False adoption and false rejection have unequal welfare costs -> encode asymmetry in minimax regret -> point-identified experiments still yield threshold rules -> test whether partial identification plus competing faces forces genuinely non-one-index decisions.

method_exemplars.technique: Certify a rule with a least-favorable prior, compute its Bayes response, match Bayes risk to worst-case regret, and use completeness to exclude rival shapes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The witness needs this two-sided verification, extended from symmetric one-index support to an unbalanced multi-face prior.

method_exemplars.technique: Search for approximate least-favorable weights by entropy mirror descent and convert dual performance into a nearly optimal testing rule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a disciplined way to locate an unbalanced finite-support prior before interval arithmetic closes exact inequalities.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed a Gaussian endpoint-game rule into a locally asymptotically minimax feasible treatment rule using regular reduced-form estimates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A certified two-dimensional witness matters for causal decisions only if its geometry transfers to the original experiment.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop convergent primal-dual certificates for compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint games over all measurable randomized rules, with certified upper and lower values and face-complete adversarial support, without requiring a complexity-rate theorem.

source_refs.claim: The paper emphasizes that unrestricted minimax-regret problems are difficult and provides analytic solutions only in structured cases.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Hedge gives epsilon-minimax rules when the statistician mixes over a fixed finite menu of decision rules, even with an infinite parameter space.
source_refs.author: Andrés Aradillas Fernández, José Blanchet, José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, Jörg Stoye, and Lezhi Tan
source_refs.venue: ACM Conference on Economics and Computation / arXiv

source_refs.claim: Simple programs are obtained only after differentiability or symmetry reduces the Gaussian game to one selected index solution.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, and Jörg Stoye

open_problems.why_unsolved: The Hedge result optimizes weights on finitely many prespecified rules, whereas the target statistician strategy is an arbitrary measurable function and Nature ranges over a continuum of endpoint states. Standard semi-infinite exchange arguments have finite-dimensional primal variables. The missing first step is therefore a reduction that preserves the measurable-rule Bayes envelope, exposes every violated endpoint face, and converts primal and dual iterates into valid global regret bounds.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit exchange or mirror-descent scheme producing certified lower and upper bounds converging to the minimax value, subsequential convergence to saddle pairs, and a verifiable face-completeness certificate for limiting adversarial support.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates computation through verifiable approximate minimaxity and ties the optimization guarantee directly to statistical risk.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact minimax rules are hard to compute -> dual optimization yields checkable approximate guarantees -> Hedge solves finite rule menus -> extend certification to unrestricted measurable rules using endpoint faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent minimax risk as convex optimization over mixture weights and use multiplicative-weight updates with a best-response oracle to close a primal-dual gap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target certificate has the same game duality but must generate decision rules and active endpoint faces instead of mixing a fixed rule dictionary.

method_exemplars.technique: Iteratively add approximately violated compact-index constraints, retain multiplier-active constraints, and prove convergence of convex semi-infinite relaxations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Endpoint faces are infinitely many regret constraints; the changed proof step is showing that the measurable-rule Bayes envelope gives separation and compactness.

method_exemplars.technique: Plug a computed Gaussian-limit optimizer and estimated covariance into the treatment problem and verify local asymptotic regret optimality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the inferential interpretation of a certified Gaussian-game solution once numerical convergence is proved.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish tie-uniform perturbation and LAN/Le Cam transfer for asymmetric polyhedral endpoint games when nuisance estimates move the Gaussian saddle correspondence across face and indexability boundaries.

source_refs.claim: The paper transfers solved limit rules in its separated smooth-asymmetric and nonsmooth-centrosymmetric regimes but leaves the joint regime open.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: For Gaussian limits, ordinary bootstrap consistency generally requires full differentiability; directional differentiability needs derivative-aware inference.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Nondifferentiable bound functionals rule out standard regular procedures and motivate local minimax analysis.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano and Jack R. Porter

open_problems.why_unsolved: At a polyhedral tie, small changes in endpoint offsets, covariance, or prior weights can change the active normal cone and create or destroy one-index optima. Pointwise convergence of one selected rule's expectation does not control data-dependent selection among multiple saddles along sequences approaching a tie. Existing treatment-choice transfers impose differentiability or recover symmetry before solving the nonsmooth game, while directional-delta theory warns that ordinary plug-in and bootstrap arguments fail at precisely these boundaries.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graph-convergence or upper-hemicontinuity theorem for the saddle correspondence, uniform over local sequences approaching every polyhedral tie, together with a feasible perturbed rule whose original-experiment maximal regret converges uniformly to the Gaussian-game value.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly separates Gaussian-limit solution from transfer to the original model and highlights regime-changing nuisance estimates.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Finite-sample causal decisions are intractable -> LAN produces a Gaussian endpoint game -> solved limit rules can be plugged back into data -> asymmetric nonsmooth ties require transfer across a set-valued solution map.

method_exemplars.technique: Use convergence of experiments, Gaussian-shift complete classes, and best-regular estimators to derive local asymptotic minimax treatment rules.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical LAN-to-treatment-decision transfer; the changed step is uniform control when the limit optimizer is nonunique and face-dependent.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate directional derivatives and use a derivative-aware resampling map when the ordinary bootstrap fails for nonsmooth functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The active-face and saddle maps are directionally but not fully differentiable at ties, so this supplies the relevant perturbation architecture.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze marginal-optimization value maps by Hadamard directional derivatives and prove local and uniform validity for supremum-type statistics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A minimax endpoint value is a marginal-optimization functional, and tie-uniform transfer must control its active argmax faces.

literature_map:
Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye (2026, arXiv:2608.09027) is the decisive boundary paper: it solves smooth asymmetry and centered nonsmoothness separately, then explicitly leaves their joint relaxation open.
Yata (2025, arXiv:2111.04926) obtains exact finite-sample Gaussian MMR rules over all measurable rules using convexity, centrosymmetry, and modulus extremizers.
Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye (2026, ReStud, arXiv:2312.17623) establish admissibility pathologies, randomization, multiplicity, and special-case failure of linear threshold rules.
Tetenov (2012, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2011.06.013) solves asymmetric Type-I/Type-II regret in point-identified experiments, but not asymmetric partial-identification geometry.
Stoye (2009, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2009.02.013) supplies exact finite-sample binary-treatment benchmarks and emphasizes their derivational difficulty.
Hirano and Porter (2009, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA6630) provide the foundational Gaussian-limit and local-asymptotic-minimax treatment-rule transfer.
Kido (2023, arXiv:2311.08958) studies local minimax treatment choice under directionally differentiable ATE bounds without solving the global asymmetric polyhedral saddle correspondence.
Christensen, Moon, and Schorfheide (2026, ReStud, doi:10.1093/restud/rdag017) derive asymptotically optimal partially identified decisions under profiled loss rather than the target unprofiled global MMR game.
Kitagawa, Lee, and Qiu (2023, Japanese Economic Review, doi:10.1007/s42973-023-00144-3) obtain logistic fractional rules for mean-square regret and leave arbitrary identified sets open.
Ishihara and Kitagawa (2021/2024, arXiv:2108.06473) study aggregation of heterogeneous experimental evidence, a concrete polyhedral and nonsmooth application.
Hirano and Porter (2012, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA8681) and Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud, arXiv:1404.3763) explain why nonsmooth ties defeat ordinary regular and bootstrap arguments.
Aradillas Fernández et al. (2025, arXiv:2509.08107) give Hedge certificates for finite rule menus, while arXiv:2511.16925 searches finite-null least-favorable distributions by mirror descent.
Zhang, Wu, and López (2010, SIAM Journal on Optimization, doi:10.1137/090767133) provide a convergent exchange template for compact convex semi-infinite constraints, but not the measurable-rule Gaussian game.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2021, Quantitative Economics, doi:10.3982/QE1609) and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1911.10215) supply near-identification and uniform directional-value-function machinery.
No located source verifies the proposed value-2/3 and tanh-perturbation witness; it remains a presolve hypothesis requiring interval-certified saddle and non-indexability checks.
